docs.title: 1. Upload genomic data and set configurations
docs.text:
• From the Home page, choose “Carrier Screening - Family. Click "Continue".
  • Input sample name, upload genomic data in compressed VCF format (.vcf.gz), and upload PED file illustrating the parents' relationship.
  • Upload customized screening panel (.txt/.tsv) or select one or more preset screening lists.
  • Select reference genome version.
  • Select variants with high sequencing quality and/or reported in ClinVar in “Variant selection".

  • Set the parameters for filtering variants in "Advanced variant filters": (global minor allele frequency, predicted scores, clinical pathogenicity).

    For explortaory analyses in the "Research options": - Polygenic risk score calculation: enter any of the PGS Catalog Identifiers if needed. - Pharmacogenomics: select to run PGx profiling or not.

    Click "Submit" to proceed.

docs.title: 2. View Results
docs.text:
The submitted job and job status are presented in "Analysis Jobs" on the homepage. \ Once the job is completed, click the job name to view all results.

FamilyRisk offers "Clinical Mode" for monogenic disease screening and clinical reporting, and "Research Mode" for exploratory analyses of complex traits by polygenic risk scores and drug response by pharmacogenomics. The results are clearly seperated with tag "CLINICAL" or "RESEARCH".

Results sections of clinical mode: - Sample & Variant Summary: This section summarizes 1) the family members' relationships from PED file; 2) the total number of screened variant and clinical P/LP variants (both ClinVar or ACMG P/LP); 3) the total number of positive findings of rare monogenic diseases and carrier status. - Screen-positive Results: This section presents the recessive disease that would be potentially transmitted to the offspring. These diseases are caused by both ClinVar and ACMG P/LP variants. - Findings by Person: This section summarises how variants are distributed across family members, covering both the variants in screen-positive findings and all screened variants. - Variant Details: This section presents all details for the filtered variants.

Results sections of research mode: - Pharmacogenomics: This section provides a report for each family member summarizing all identified pharmacogenomics diplotypes in the newborns via PharmCat. Detailed explanations and recommendations are illustrated in the structured report. - Polygenic Risk Scores: This section provides polygenic scores of each family member and reference population regarding the required PGS model. The similarity scores are also provided for genetic clustering. Information is also summarized into a strctured report.

docs.title: 3. Choose pathogenic variants and potential diseases to be included in the final PDF report.
docs.text:
FamilyRisk provides a template for clinical reporting, where users can further customize the report by selecting specific results and adding professional advice, suggestions, and comments. 1) In "Screen-positive Results", "Disease Carrier Status", and "Variant Details" sections, switch the button under "Include" to include or exclude the specific variant to be presented in the final report.

2) Click "Report Generation" to generate the report.

3) Add additional analytical texts, recommendations, and references via the portal. 4) Set the report language. Options: English, Turkish, Spanish, Korean, Chinese, Japanese. 5) Click "Continue" to view the final digital report.

6) Download, print, or re-edit the report following the previous steps.

docs.title: 4. Export Data
docs.text:
• Results in each section could be downloaded separately.
  • All results could be wrapped up and downloaded as a zipped file by clicking the download button in the bottom-right corner.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: The FamilyRisk database is a unified resource for carrier and newborn screening. It could be found under "Database" on the homepage.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The database information is summarized in the "Overview". It integrates 3,112 curated gene–disease associations derived from seven leading NBSeq projects and two ACMG recommendations, collectively covering 15 disease ontologies.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: Each of the projects collected in this database could be reviewed in the "Projects". By clicking the project name/logo, project information, filtering criteria for pathogenic variants, clinical returned results, and quick links to the official website and relevant publications can be referred to. More importantly, the detailed screening list of each project is presented as well.

docs.title: Screening Results
docs.text: The clinical returned results of five newborn sequencing projects are summarized in the "Screening Results". Notably, only BabySeq and EarlyCheck disclosed the screen-positive carrier status.

docs.title: Generator
docs.text: FamilyRisk Database offers the Screening List Generator, enabling users to customize gene-disease associations outside the collections. This tool displays all curated associations collected in the database, with the corresponding disease inheritance modes, OMIM identifiers, disease ontologies, originating projects, and GenCC classifications and submitters. Users could select subgroups of the screening lists and disease inheritance modes via “Advanced Filters”. Additional gene-disease associations could be manually added into the full list via the “Quick Add Custom Entry” function by specifying the gene symbol, disease name, and other relevant details. All customized entries will be added to the end of the main table, while the wrong ones could be easily cleared. Eventually, the full list or selected associations could be downloaded locally and applied to the downstream genomic data analysis in the main portal.

docs.title: FamilyRiskAI
docs.text:
FamilyRiskAI is the AI chatbox of FamilyRisk, built for the clinical geneticists, genetic counselors and researchers who use the web server. Through natural-language conversation, it helps users explore the screening knowledge base, build customized screening lists, configure analyses, and quickly understand the results of finished analyses.FamilyRiskAI does not provide a diagnosis, prognosis or treatment recommendation. All screening findings need confirmation and interpretation by a genetic counselor or clinical geneticist.

FamilyRiskAI can be opened from the purple button (✦) in the bottom-right corner of the homepage.

docs.title: 1. Explore the screening knowledge base
docs.text:
FamilyRiskAI finds genes, diseases and preset panels in the curated screening list. It searches the gene–disease associations, each with its inheritance mode, disorder group and GenCC validity, and it describes and compares the 18 preset panels, including their contents and overlap.

Example questions:

  • "Which preset panels include CFTR?"
  • "What is the inheritance mode and GenCC validity of IDH3A?"
  • "How do the BabySeq and EarlyCheck panels differ?"

docs.title: 2. Build customized screening lists
docs.text:
FamilyRiskAI assembles custom gene panels from the curated list. Only genes from the curated list are accepted: a gene outside the list is reported as such rather than added. The proposed panel arrives as a card that can be applied to the analysis form, or downloaded as a gene list, with one click.

Example question:

  • "Build a panel of autosomal recessive metabolic disorders with definitive GenCC validity."

docs.title: 3. Configure analyses and filtering options
docs.text:
FamilyRiskAI explains each analysis and drafts its configuration, including the optional filtering parameters. It reads each analysis's live parameters with their defaults and allowed values, and checks every suggested configuration against them. The proposed configuration arrives as a card that the user can apply to the analysis form with one click.

Example questions:

  • "What parameters can I set for family-level carrier screening, and what are their defaults?"
  • "Set up a newborn screening analysis using the ACMG secondary findings panel."

docs.title: 4. Pinpoint, summarise and explain variants
docs.text:
FamilyRiskAI reads the results of your own finished analyses and of the six public demo analyses. It helps you quickly pinpoint variants of interest, and summarises and explains the findings.

Example questions:

  • "Summarise the screen-positive findings of my newborn screening demo."
  • "Which variants in this family analysis are in autosomal recessive genes?"

docs.title: A Free-Access, Integrated Web Server for Early-Life Disease Screening and Clinical Reporting
docs.text: 📍 Access FamilyRisk: https://www.phenomeportal.org/familyrisk

docs.title: 1️⃣ Comprehensive Screening Database
docs.text:
FamilyRisk integrates curated knowledge on screening strategies, gene–disease associations, and clinical outcomes to support screening study design and clinical decision-making.

The database aggregates evidence from seven established newborn sequencing initiatives (BabySeq, BabyScreen+, BabyDetect, GUARDIAN, EarlyCheck, Genomics 101, NBScreening), ACMG Secondary Findings, and ACMG Expanded Carrier Screening.

docs.title: 2️⃣ Flexible Panel Customization
docs.text:
The Screening List Generator embedded in the database allows users to:

  • Select preset screening lists
  • Add or remove gene–disease associations
  • Create customized panels tailored to specific clinical or research needs

This feature supports adaptable implementation across diverse screening scenarios.

docs.title: 3️⃣ Versatile Genomic Analysis
docs.text: FamilyRisk streamlines genomic analysis at the individual, family, and population level. It supports interpretation of small variants (SNVs/indels), copy number variants, and structural variants. Compatible with both GRCh37 and GRCh38 reference genomes.

docs.title: 4️⃣ Segregation Analysis
docs.text: FamilyRisk provides integrated segregation analysis to evaluate inheritance patterns and assess transmission of pathogenic variants within families.

docs.title: 5️⃣ Polygenic Risk Evaluation & Pharmacogenomics Profiling
docs.text: FamilyRisk enables polygenic score (PGS) evaluation for complex diseases and common traits. It also compares individual's PGS against the reference populations to estimate genetic susceptibility. It phases Pharmacogenomic (PGx) diplotype to provide Evidence-based therapeutic recommendations.

docs.title: 6️⃣ Flexible Clinical Reporting
docs.text:
FamilyRisk separates results into structured sub-panels for clarity and usability.

Users can:

  • Select specific variants or diseases
  • Generate customizable clinical PDF reports
  • Add professional comments, clinical interpretations, and recommendations

This facilitates translation from genomic data to actionable clinical documentation.

docs.title: 📘 Tutorials
docs.text:
• The step-by-step video tutorial could be found:
  • [Video]

Each function of FamilyRisk is documented with step-by-step Markdown guides:

Function Description Tutorial Database Integrated knowledge of carrier and newborn screening projects, gene panels, and clinical outcomes. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-Individual Individual-level newborn screening. Identify potential monogenic rare diseases and disease carrier status. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-Family Family-level newborn screening. Identify potential monogenic rare diseases and disease carrier status in the newborns. Segregation analysis to visualize variant inheritance patterns. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-Population Cohort-level newborn screening. Identify regional prevalent monogenic rare diseases and disease carrier status. Calculate cohort-level allele frequency. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-CNV/SV Annotate individual-level copy number variants and structural variants in the newborn. View Tutorial Carrier Screening-Individual Individual-level carrier screening. Identify potential recessive diseases that might inherit by the offspring. View Tutorial Carrier Screening-Family Couple-level carrier screening. Identify potential recessive diseases that might inherit by the offspring. View Tutorial

docs.title: Homepage
docs.text: The FamilyRisk homepage is the starting point for all analyses. It can be accessed at https://www.phenomeportal.org/familyrisk. No account or registration is needed.

docs.title: Navigation Bar
docs.text:
The navigation bar at the top of the page gives access to the main sections of FamilyRisk:

Tab Description Home The homepage, where users submit new analyses and review existing analysis jobs. API Information on the FamilyRisk REST API for submitting and retrieving analyses programmatically. Database The FamilyRisk screening knowledge base and the Screening List Generator (see Database). Help Help and guidance for using FamilyRisk. Settings User settings for the web server.

docs.title: Analysis Jobs
docs.text:
The "Analysis Jobs" panel on the left lists all analyses submitted from your browser, together with the public demo analyses. Analyses are linked to your browser's access token and are visible only to you.

  • Search and filter: jobs can be searched by name in the search box, and filtered by job status via the drop-down menu (default: All).
  • Job card: each job shows its name, analysis type and current status. Clicking a job opens its results.
  • Job status:
Status Description Pending The job has been created but not yet submitted for analysis. Queued The job has been submitted and is waiting for an available analysis worker. Running The analysis is in progress. Completed The analysis has finished and the results are ready to view and download. Failed The analysis did not finish successfully.
  • ⓘ shows the details of the job.
  • Download (⤓) downloads the results of the job.

docs.title: Demo analyses
docs.text:
Six public demo analyses, marked with a DEMO tag, are provided on Genome in a Bottle (GIAB) reference genomes, one for each analysis type. They show the complete output of each analysis without uploading any data, and are a good starting point for new users.

Demo Analysis type Newborn screening Newborn Screening Carrier screening Carrier Screening Couple carrier screening Carrier Screening - Family Newborn family screening Newborn Screening - Family Newborn cohort screening Newborn Screening - Cohort CNV/SV analysis CNV/SV Analysis

docs.title: New Analysis
docs.text:
The "New Analysis" panel on the right is where new analyses are started. Clicking a card opens the submission form for that analysis.

Analysis Description Tutorial Newborn Screening Newborn inherited-risk screening for one individual across the FamilyRisk gene panels. Newborn Screening - Individual Carrier Screening Carrier screening for recessive conditions for one individual across the FamilyRisk gene panels. Carrier Screening - Individual Newborn Screening - Family Newborn inherited-risk screening for one pedigree, with optional pharmacogenomics (PGx), polygenic risk score (PRS) and imputation. Newborn Screening - Family Newborn Screening - Cohort Population or cohort newborn screening from a multi-sample VCF and sample metadata. Newborn Screening - Population Carrier Screening - Family Carrier screening for one pedigree, from a merged family VCF or one VCF per person. Carrier Screening - Family CNV/SV Analysis Structural variant and copy number variant analysis with AnnotSV, with optional SNV/indel input to detect compound heterozygosity. Newborn Screening - CNV & SV

docs.title: FamilyRiskAI
docs.text:
The purple button (✦) in the bottom-right corner opens FamilyRiskAI, the AI chatbox of FamilyRisk (see FamilyRiskAI). Through natural-language conversation, it helps users explore the screening knowledge base, build customized screening lists and set optional filtering options, quickly pinpoint variants of interest, and summarise and explain the variants found.

!! Note FamilyRisk and FamilyRiskAI do not provide a diagnosis, prognosis or treatment recommendation. All screening findings need confirmation and interpretation by a genetic counselor or clinical geneticist.

docs.text:

  • Upload customized screening panel (.txt/.tsv) or select one or more preset screening lists.

  • Select variant type. Options: CNV, SV.
  • Click "Submit" to proceed.

The newborn screening of population level is for research purpose only, with each section tagged as "RESEARCH".

Results sections: - Sample & Variant Summary: This section summarizes the total number of screened newborns, filtered variants, and the screened ClinVar P/LP variants. - Screen-positive Results: This section presents the potential monogenic rare diseases identified in all newborns. These diseases are caused by both ClinVar and ACMG P/LP variants. - Disease Carrier Status: This section presents the potential disease carriers identified in all newborns. These diseases are caused by both ClinVar and ACMG P/LP variants, which are heterozygous states and associated with recessive diseases. - Statistics: - Pathogenic variant stats: The total number of pathogenic variants that associated with screen-positive or carrier status findings. - Ontology stats: the total number of diseases that associated with screen-positive or carrier status findings. - Cohort-level allele frequency: the allele frequency of each identified variant within the cohort. - Variant Details: This section presents all details for the filtered variants. - Pharmacogenomics: This section provides a report for each family member summarizing all identified pharmacogenomics diplotypes in the newborns via PharmCat. Detailed explanations and recommendations are illustrated in the structured report. - Polygenic Risk Scores: This section provides polygenic scores of each family member and reference population regarding the required PGS model.
